{"R1": {"R1P1": {"snippet_ids": ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5", "S6"], "text": "Orchard handles a supplier invoice by first receiving it in the shared invoice mailbox by the accounts payable coordinator. The coordinator checks that each invoice names a supplier and purchase order, then enters it in the ledger with status Received. Missing purchase order details are returned to the supplier for correction; the invoice does not enter the approval queue until corrected. For invoices with complete intake details, the coordinator attaches the original invoice to the ledger record and routes the record to the budget owner named on the purchase order. The budget owner compares the invoice amount with the purchase order and confirms that the goods or services were received. If both checks pass, the owner marks the invoice Approved in the ledger. A mismatch is sent back to accounts payable for investigation, rather than being approved automatically. Approval is the budget owner's decision. ", "status": "supported"}, "R1P2": {"snippet_ids": ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5", "S6"], "text": "Each stage of the supplier invoice process is owned by specific roles. The accounts payable coordinator owns the receipt stage, as they are responsible for receiving and initially processing the invoice. The budget owner owns the approval stage, as they are responsible for confirming the invoice amount and goods/services received. The treasury specialist owns the payment stage, as they are responsible for including approved invoices in the payment run and recording the payment reference in the ledger.", "status": "supported"}}}
